# Plan: Unattended SPE rounds, starting at round 5

## What this plan covers

You approve this plan once, tonight. That approval covers round 5 in full. It also covers the rules I follow for round 6 and later. You will not see the plans for rounds 6 and later before they run. So I will mark those plans and predictions as my own defaults, not as plans you approved.

I will not push, deploy, or send anything. I will make local commits after each SPE step, because you asked for that. Tags stay local. Commit messages will carry no Claude attribution lines.

## Overnight limits (my defaults, logged in `spe/spec/disagreements.md`)

| Limit | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Most rounds tonight | 4 (rounds 5, 6, 7, 8) | Each round needs a close-out before the next respec. Four rounds leave time for one rerun if a gate fails. |
| Paid spend per round | 1.5 times the measured cost of round 4 | Round 4 is the latest real cost figure. The margin covers extra trials on split cells. |
| Paid spend for the night | 4 times the measured cost of round 4 | This stops the loop before cost grows without a check from you. |
| Wall clock | No new round starts after 06:00 local time | You get a finished report in the morning, not a run in progress. |
| Prediction match | A cell matches when the measured value is within the tolerance stated in that row. The default tolerance is 5 percentage points for rates and 15 percent for counts and costs. | The stop rule needs a fixed test. I set it before any result exists. |

Trials that would cross a spend cap are skipped. Each skip goes in the round's results with the reason.

## Round 5

### Before planning (read only)

1. Read `spe/spec/spec.md`, the "Proposed for round 5" table, and `spe/predictions/r04-draft.yaml`.
2. Read `spe/prediction-log.md` and `spe/failures.md` for rounds 1 to 4.
3. Read `spe/spec/disagreements.md` for open decisions that have an owner.

If an open decision is owned by you and round 5 depends on it, I will not guess. I will skip that change, log it as open, and run round 5 without it.

### Specify

- I save your message from tonight word for word in `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r05.md`.
- I add a round 5 requirement table to `spe/spec/spec.md` with the columns ID, Requirement, Source, and Test.
- Each row in "Proposed for round 5" becomes a row, or I reject it with a reason. Sources are your words, a logged decision, or a failure ID such as "r04 F7".
- Each configuration changes one thing from the round 4 baseline.
- Commit: `SPE r05 specify`.

### Predict

- I start from `spe/predictions/r04-draft.yaml`. Every number starts as "same as last round". I move a number only when I can write the reason in one line.
- The table has one row per metric and one column per configuration. Every cell holds a number. Each row names the grader check that measures it and gives a one-line Why.
- I copy this plan to `spe/plans/r05.md`.
- I write `spe/predictions/r05.yaml`. It starts with `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.` It holds the round, the date, the author ("Claude, approved by the user in plan mode"), the configs, the numbers, a Why per number, and `same_as_last_round` per number.
- Commit: `SPE r05 predict: <one-line summary of what changed from r04>`. This commit lands before any harness work.

### Evaluate

The harness lives in `spe/evals/harness/r05-workflow.js`. The round number is held in one `ROUND` constant. Prompt text reads it from there.

Gates before launch. Each gate must pass, or the round halts.

1. Grader selftest. The oracle answer passes. An empty answer fails. A known wrong answer fails.
2. Control. I regrade the round 4 outputs with the round 5 grader. The scores must match the logged round 4 scores within tolerance. If they do not match, the grader changed meaning, and I treat that as a broken grader.
3. Dry run on 2 or 3 cells. I check that trials return valid output for the schema and stay under the per-trial cost cap.

Run rules.

- Each trial returns output that fits a schema. Code checks run first. A judge model scores only what code cannot check.
- Trials cannot read graders, answer keys, or prediction files. After the run I scan each transcript for reads of those paths. I void any trial that touched them.
- Cells with split results get extra trials, up to a cap of 2 times the base trial count for that cell.
- The workflow ends with a failure analysis step and a completeness critic step.

Cost estimate. I will give an estimate from round 4 cost scaled by the trial count. I will label it as unmeasured.

Commits: `SPE r05 evaluate (harness)` before launch. `SPE r05 evaluate (results): <headline>` after the completion notice arrives.

### Learn

The workflow returns at launch. I start close-out only when its completion notice arrives.

- `spe/prediction-log.md` gets a row per cell with Metric, Config, Predicted, Measured, Same as last round, Verdict, and Closer. Under the table, "Which Why broke" quotes each missed Why and names the wrong assumption. If "same as last round" beat my moved numbers, I say so plainly.
- `spe/failures.md` gets each new failure type with its name, kind, round, What, How to spot it, Seen in, and Fix. A grader bug found after the run counts as a failure. I keep the original and regraded numbers side by side.
- `spe/spec/spec.md` gets a "Proposed for round 6" table.
- I write `spe/predictions/r05-draft.yaml` with `status: draft`.
- I update `spe/README.md`.
- Commit: `SPE r05 learn: <headline>`. Local tag: `spe-r05`.

## Rounds 6 to 8

Each round repeats the same five steps as round 5, with three differences.

1. **No new user input.** The transcript file for the round records "No user input this round. Autonomous round under the plan approved on 2026-10-21." I do not invent user words.
2. **Proposals become defaults.** I adopt or reject each "Proposed for round N" row myself. I log each choice in `spe/spec/disagreements.md` as a default with its reason. Any proposal that changes scope, the task set, the budget, or what counts as passing is a decision only you can make. I leave it open and do not run it.
3. **Author line.** Plans and predictions for these rounds name the author as "Claude, autonomous default under the 2026-10-21 plan. Not reviewed by the user."

I never edit a saved prediction after a trial in that round has run.

## When the loop stops

I stop starting new rounds when any of these is true.

| Condition | What I do |
|---|---|
| Predictions matched results for 3 rounds in a row | Stop. The method has converged for this task set. |
| Every configuration passed every check | Stop. I write a proposal for harder tasks or stricter graders and leave it open for you. I do not change the task set alone. |
| A spend cap or the 06:00 cutoff would be crossed | Stop before the round starts. |
| A grader gate fails, the control regrade drifts, or an answer key leaked into a trial | Halt. I void the affected trials, log the failure, and write up what I found. |
| The next round needs a decision only you can make | Halt and log the decision with you as owner. |
| The same failure type shows up two rounds in a row after a fix | Halt. Another round would spend money without new evidence. |

## Morning report

I will leave the report in chat and in `spe/README.md`. It will contain these parts.

- One headline per round.
- A table of prediction accuracy by round. It shows the share of cells that matched, and whether "same as last round" beat my moved numbers.
- Total spend against the caps, with every skipped trial listed.
- Each halt and its reason, if one happened.
- Open decisions that need you, each with the options and my suggested default.
- The list of local commits and tags. None of them are pushed.

## What I will not do tonight

- Push commits or tags, open PRs, deploy, or send messages.
- Change the task set, the budget caps, or the pass threshold.
- Edit a prediction after its round has started running.
- Count a voided trial in any result.
